findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed TCS vegetables to be resting on prep table at 70F. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled 2 hours before and are in use as orders come in. Education was provided on proper cold holding expectations, and facility will be using a Time as Control for the vegetables. PIC is unsure if this will be a permanent addition, however inspector provided facility with paperwork and education if facility would like to continue. Ensure any TCS item is being cold held below 41F or discarded after 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and items were dated. Ensure after 24 hours, any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is date marked and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed TCS item in walk in cooler to be resting on floor. Discussed with PIC, items were moved to at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any TCS item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed knives on magnetic wall strip to be in contact with a soiled clipboard. Discussed with PIC, clipboard was moved away from wall strip and knives were placed through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process. Ensure clean utensils are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers of TCS foods missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, a majority of the TCS foods are prepped daily and disposed of at the end of the day, however chicken and crab rangoons were prepared yesterday (8/22/24). Date marking stickers were placed on containers, ensure any TCS foods being kept longer than 24 hours are properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed large accumulation of grease along the fryer sides and sides of the prep table/wok area near the fryer. Flooring underneath and behind the fryer has grease layer. The equipment needs pulled out and scrubbed, as well as the flooring behind the fryer. Use de-greaser to cut the grease and wash, rinse, sanitize. Discussed with PIC to best of ability (language barrier). PIC seemed to understand. Indicated new equipment will be put in. Clean by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of caulking: mop sink is missing caulking (caulk sink to wall), women’s bathroom hand sink needs re-caulked (coming away from wall and sink), and the coving at the base of the walk-in cooler needs caulked to the wall (gaps where grout and caulking should be). Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The walk in cooler is not currently functioning during this inspection. PIC is aware and has already contacted Element Services in Chatham to replace the equipment. TCS foods are still observed in the  unit at this time (refer to line item #22). Inspector contacted element services and discussed with the owner. The items needing to be replaced were ordered Monday and should be in in the middle of next week (approximately Nov. 22-23). Element services stated that they would be installing the equipment the next day after the equipment are received. Inspector will follow-up next week for completed repairs.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

On arrival, the hand sink in the kitchen has a large box of food on top of it blocking use. The box was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Multiple TCS items in the walk in cooler are observed with temperatures between 55F-58F. The cooler is not currently functioning correctly (refer to line item #1). A translator was contacted by the PIC to facilitate effective communication. The foods were received and then cooked approximately 3 hours prior to the conversation taking place. Foods were moved to the other freezers/coolers in the facility to correct the violation. Ice was available in the walk-in cooler, but was not sufficient for the needs at this time.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. 

Throughout the inspection, two sanitizer rags are observed on the counter throughout the inspection. Rags were moved to a bucket, once it was made, to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival, no sanitizers were made up and ready for use in the facility. When pointed out, the PIC created a bucket of sanitizer to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).  

A 5 gallon bucket of sauce is observed under a sink in the kitchen. Foods should not be stored under drain lines. The bucket was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The broccoli pan in the left prep cooler is observed soiled during the inspection. This cooler does not have adequate temperature control, as noted on previous inspections, to prevent any pathogenic growth/contamination. PIC instructed to maintain clean, and moved the pan to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

No date marking is observed on the RTE items in the walk in cooler. A conversation was attempted in relation to date marking the Ready-To-Eat (RTE) foods in the cooler and a hand out (in English) was given to the PIC. Date marks were added to the items in the walk in to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Multiple non-food contact surfaces are observed in need of cleaning. Items include: 1) the outside of a pan of onions in the walk in cooler; 2) the lids of multiple 5 gallon sauce containers in the walk in cooler. PIC instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation of filth on the containers.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The floor of the walk in cooler is in need of cleaning, specifically under the shelves and inn the corners. A yellow/green liquid is observed as well as food debris. PIC instructed to maintain clean.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
(REPEAT PRACTICE) 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. 

Cooked noodles are observed in the left prep cooler holding at 51F-54F internal temperature. The rest of the cooler is observed at a similar temperature (both the top prep area and the space underneath. PIC indicated that the noodles had been in the cooler a total of 3 hours at the time of the inspection.  The noodles will be discarded at 5pm  and the PIC is instructed to only store non-TCS foods there (vegetables were suggested).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. 

A butcher knife is observed stored in a crack between the table in the kitchen area and the prep cooler. This crack is not easily clean able and should not be used for storing food contact items. The knife was moved to cleaning during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. 

Cooked noodles are observed in the left prep cooler holding at 60F internal temperature. The rest of the cooler is observed at a similar temperature (both the top prep area and the space underneath. The noodles were discarded to correct and the PIC is instructed to only store non-TCS foods there (vegetables were suggested).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival, no sanitizer solutions were observed in the facility. PIC is instructed to ensure that sanitizers are available at al times that prep and handling are taking place. A solution was made during the inspection to correct.

findings.comment: 3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).  A 5 gallon bucket of sauce is observed under a sink in the kitchen. Foods should not be stored under drain lines. The bucket was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.comment:
4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. 
A butcher knife is observed stored in a crack between the table in the kitchen area and the prep cooler. This crack is not easily clean able and should not be used for storing food contact items. The knife was moved to cleaning during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: 4-101.19: Non-FOOD CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, non-absorbent, and SMOOTH material. 1) The shelf under the counter that holds wontons has paint that is starting to chip and is exposing the wood underneath. 2) The corner of the service counter as you are moving between the kitchen and seating area is observed with exposed wood showing that appears to be soiled. 3) Cardboard is being used under the service counter. Cardboard is an absorbent material and should not be used in food service areas. The Person In Charge (PIC) is instructed to either use Plexiglas or paint the surfaces to ensure that they remain smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Foods should be maintained at 41°F, or less. Cooked noodles and sliced onions in the prep cooler closest to the dry storage are registering at 53 on the inspector's probe thermometer. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. The prep cooler was stocked at 10:00 am this morning. Noodles and onions will be used or discarded by 4:00 pm this afternoon. PIC is instructed to adjust the cooler or prepare a time control policy for the cooler.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. # knives are observed stored in a crack between the table in the sink area and the wall of the walk in cooler. This crack is not easily clean able and should not be used for storing food contact items. The knives were moved to cleaning during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) Raw chicken is observed stored above carrots in the walk in cooler. The carrots were moved across the cooler to be in the vegitable section. A handout in chinese was given to the owner stating the correc storage order for different types of foods in a cooler.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Mold was observed on two food container lids in the walk in cooler. Mold was not observed iin the containers or in the foods. The lids were cleaned during the insepction to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Raw peppers were observed below raw chicken in the walk in cooler. The peppers and chicken were moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) A spatula was observed stored in sauce so that the hand contact portion was partially submerged in the sauce. The scoop was removed during the inspection. Inspector suggested separating batches of sauce so that the food line is bellow the handle of the spatulas used for stirring the sauce during prep.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 (C) EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS or other items needing protection can not result.

A coffee cup was observed on the steam table and a glass on the counter by the woks. Neither item has a straw and the cup was without a lid. Inspector discussed the situation with the PIC and instructed them to store beverages in areas separate from food preparation. The cups were moved during the inspection.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 (C) During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored in the FOOD with their handles above the top of the FOOD and the container, on a cleaned and sanitized surface, in running water or in water held at 135 F or higher.

A scoop was observed stored in a bucket of sauce so that only a small piece was out of the sauce. Discussed with the PIC and the scoop was moved to cleaning during the inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 (C) Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The container used for storing one of the rice scoops was observed with a thick layer of grease in the bottom underneath where a cup is used for direct contact with the scoop. Discussed general cleaning with the PIC and instructed to maintain clean.
